references.text: Context for covering the face with a veil; Moses covered his face after speaking to the Israelites
Continuation of the description of Moses' radiant face and the use of the veil
Moses spoke with the Lord face to face in the tent of meeting, a parallel to entering into the presence of the Lord
God speaks with Moses face to face and not in riddles, confirming Moses' unique relationship with the Lord
There was no prophet like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face
Paul uses Moses' veil as an allegory; the veil is removed when one turns to the Lord (ἡνίκα δὲ ἐὰν ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς κύριον, περιαιρεῖται τὸ κάλυμμα)
Believers see the Lord's glory with unveiled faces, in contrast to the veil Moses used
Confirms the consistent prophetic model where Moses delivered God's words exactly as they were given.
A clear literary parallel that underscores the continuity of Moses' leadership and God's unchanging message.
Complementary verses that together describe Moses' unique 'face-to-face' communication and the need for a veil before the people.
